answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The plume multiplier is published, charged in walnut, and saffron lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3277 identities would post 1270 proofs and burn roughly 17 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
